name: TA-9-dsm-obstruction
why: A flat, fully-supported terrain with an above-ground DSM return (heightAboveGround) over two cells of column 2, at rows 1 and 2, both exceeding the declared obstacleHeightThreshold, forcing a detour into row 3 — pinning that obstruction blocking (not step height or NoData) is what closes these two cells. Unlike TA-4's single-row detour, the flat terrain gives the bypass a genuine 4-way tie (enumerated by brute force over the whole grid): dropping into row 3 either diagonally or straight down at column 1, and climbing back out of row 3 either diagonally or straight across at column 3, are all equal-cost combinations, so this fixture is compared on cost/length/eligibility rather than an exact path.
